project.name: Modular Synth Demo
project.notes: Modular Synth Demo Press the green flag. One script wires the Modular Synth library's ready-made modules into a patch and plays it for 24 seconds while an oscilloscope on the stage draws the sound. Lead voice: the Note Sequencer sets the pitch of Oscillator 1 (saw). Filter 1 (low pass) shapes the tone, with LFO 1 slowly sweeping the cutoff. ADSR 1, gated by the Trigger Sequencer, opens Volume 1 on each step marked x. Bass voice: the Slew Limiter smooths the Note Sequencer's pitch so Oscillator 2 (square) glides between notes. The Audio Divider drops it an octave, and the Waveform Processor adds harmonics, with LFO 2 moving the fold. The Trigger Divider passes every second trigger to ADSR 2, which opens Volume 2. Hi-hat: white Noise through Filter 2 (high pass), shaped by an envelope and volume made with the Create block. Mix joins the three voices and feeds the Delay, which goes to the speaker. Change a number in any Set block and press the green flag again to hear the difference. Each module's settings are visible in its variable.

block-definition.comment: Makes a new module and puts it in a variable with the given name. The variable then stands for the module in every other block; its watcher shows the settings. The library comes with ready-made modules: Oscillator 1, Oscillator 2, Filter 1, Filter 2, ADSR 1, ADSR 2, LFO 1, LFO 2, Volume 1, Volume 2, Delay, Noise, Ring Modulator, Waveform Processor, Audio Divider, Slew Limiter, Trigger Divider, Trigger Sequencer, Note Sequencer and Keyboard. Use Create only when more are needed. oscillator: produces a tone. Settings: wave type (saw, square, triangle or sine), frequency (Hz; 440 is the A above middle C), pulse width (1 to 99 %; the share of each cycle the square wave spends high, 50 is an even square; other waves ignore it), control (a module whose signal bends the frequency, in semitones), trigger (a module whose rising signal restarts the wave). filter: keeps the low part of a sound (low pass) or the high part (high pass). Settings: type, cutoff (Hz), resonance (0 to 100 %; emphasis at the cutoff, singing on its own above 80; starts at 100), input (the module whose sound is filtered), control (a module whose signal moves the cutoff, in semitones). ADSR: an envelope, a control signal that rises when its gate opens and falls when it closes. Settings: attack (seconds to climb to the peak), decay (seconds to fall to the sustain level), sustain (% of the peak held while the gate is open), release (seconds to fall to zero after the gate closes), amount (the peak: semitones at a control jack, % at a level jack), gate (a module whose signal opens the gate, or empty to use the gate block). volume: makes a sound louder or softer. Settings: level (0 to 100 %, the loudness with nothing in control), input (the module whose sound is adjusted), control (a module whose signal adds to the level, in %; an ADSR with amount 100 and level 0 makes notes start and stop). LFO: a slow repeating control signal. Settings: wave type (saw, square, triangle or sine, the shape of the motion), speed (cycles per second), amount (the swing each way: semitones at a control jack, % at a level jack), trigger (a module whose rising signal restarts the cycle). Amount 1 into an oscillator's control gives vibrato, 50 into a volume's control gives tremolo, 24 into a filter's control gives a wah. delay: repeats a sound as echoes. Settings: time (seconds between echoes), repeats (0 to 95 %, how much each echo feeds the next), blend (0 to 100 %, share of echo in the output), input. noise: white noise as a sound, or random steps as a control signal. Settings: noise type (white or random steps), speed (steps per second), amount (the swing: semitones at a control jack, % at a level jack, 1 for full noise), trigger (a module whose rising signal picks a new step). ring modulator: multiplies two sounds, giving bell-like tones. Settings: input, input 2. waveform processor: folds the peaks of a sound back on themselves, adding harsh overtones; a control jack lets an envelope or LFO move the fold. Settings: fold (0 to 100 ％), input, control (adds ％ to fold). audio divider: a square wave one, two or three octaves below the input. Settings: octaves (1 to 3), input. slew limiter: smooths a control signal, so steps become slides. Settings: rise and fall (seconds), input. trigger divider: passes every n-th gate it receives. Settings: divide by (1 to 16), trigger. trigger sequencer: a repeating pattern of gates. Settings: pattern (text; x is a gate, . is a rest), tempo (steps per minute), clock (a module whose rising signal advances a step; empty to use the tempo). note sequencer: a repeating row of notes as a pitch signal. Settings: notes (MIDI note numbers separated by spaces; 69 is A 440, which is 0 at a pitch control), tempo, clock. Plug it into an oscillator's control. Give a note sequencer and a trigger sequencer the same clock, such as a square LFO, to keep them in step. keyboard: plays notes from the computer keyboard or a MIDI device. Settings: source, lowest note. It has three outputs, which appear in jack dropdowns as "Keyboard: pitch", "Keyboard: gate" and "Keyboard: velocity". The settings are saved with the project. After loading, a module is rebuilt from them the next time a block uses it.

inputs.input: oscillatoroscillator filter ADSR volume LFO delay noise ring modulator waveform processor audio divider slew limiter trigger divider trigger sequencer note sequencer keyboard

block-definition.s: Set Oscillator %'module' $nl Wave Type: %'wave type' $nl Frequency: %'frequency' Hz $nl Control: %'control' $nl Trigger: %'trigger' $nl Pulse Width: %'pulse width' ％
block-definition.comment: Sets up an oscillator, the module that produces a tone. Wave Type: saw, square, triangle or sine Frequency: Hz; 440 is the A above middle C Control: a module whose signal bends the frequency, in semitones Trigger: a module whose rising signal restarts the wave Pulse Width: 1 to 99 ％, the share of each cycle the square wave spends high; other waves ignore it An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Filter %'module' $nl Type: %'type' $nl Input: %'input' $nl Cutoff: %'cutoff' Hz $nl Resonance: %'resonance' ％ $nl Control: %'control'
block-definition.comment: Sets up a filter. Type: low pass keeps the sound below the cutoff, high pass keeps the sound above it Input: the module whose sound is filtered Cutoff: Hz Resonance: 0 to 100 ％; emphasis at the cutoff, singing on its own above 80 Control: a module whose signal moves the cutoff, in semitones An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set ADSR %'module' $nl Attack: %'attack' s $nl Decay: %'decay' s $nl Sustain: %'sustain' ％ $nl Release: %'release' s $nl Amount: %'amount' $nl Gate: %'gate'
block-definition.comment: Sets up an ADSR envelope, a control signal that rises when its gate opens and falls when it closes. Attack: seconds to climb to the peak Decay: seconds to fall to the sustain level Sustain: ％ of the peak held while the gate is open Release: seconds to fall to zero after the gate closes Amount: the peak; semitones at a control jack, ％ at a level jack Gate: a module whose signal opens the gate, or empty to use the Gate block An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

Sets up a volume module. Input: the module whose sound is adjusted Level: 0 to 100 ％, the loudness with nothing in Control Control: a module whose signal adds to the level, in ％; an ADSR with amount 100 and level 0 makes notes start and stop An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set LFO %'module' $nl Wave Type: %'wave type' $nl Speed: %'speed' Hz $nl Amount: %'amount' $nl Trigger: %'trigger'
block-definition.comment: Sets up an LFO, a slow repeating control signal. Wave Type: the shape of the motion Speed: cycles per second Amount: the swing each way; semitones at a control jack, ％ at a level jack Trigger: a module whose rising signal restarts the cycle An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Delay %'module' $nl Input: %'input' $nl Time: %'time' s $nl Repeats: %'repeats' ％ $nl Blend: %'blend' ％
block-definition.comment: Sets up a delay, which repeats a sound as echoes. Input: the module whose sound is echoed Time: seconds between echoes Repeats: 0 to 95 ％, how much of each echo feeds the next Blend: 0 to 100 ％, the share of echo in the output An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Noise %'module' $nl Noise Type: %'noise type' $nl Speed: %'speed' Hz $nl Amount: %'amount' $nl Trigger: %'trigger'
block-definition.comment: Sets up a noise module. Noise Type: white (a hiss, for sound) or random steps (a stepped random control signal) Speed: new random steps per second Amount: the swing; semitones at a control jack, ％ at a level jack; 1 gives full-strength noise as a sound Trigger: a module whose rising signal picks a new random step An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

Sets up a ring modulator, which multiplies two sounds into bell-like tones. Input, Input 2: the two modules whose sounds are multiplied An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Waveform Processor %'module' $nl Input: %'input' $nl Fold: %'fold' ％ $nl Control: %'control'
block-definition.comment: Sets up a waveform processor, which folds the peaks of a sound back on themselves to add harmonics; the fold can be moved by another module. Input: the module whose sound is folded Fold: 0 to 100 ％ Control: a module whose signal adds ％ to the fold An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

Sets up an audio divider, which makes a square wave below the input. Input: the module whose sound sets the pitch Octaves: 1, 2 or 3 octaves down An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Slew Limiter %'module' $nl Input: %'input' $nl Rise: %'rise' s $nl Fall: %'fall' s
block-definition.comment: Sets up a slew limiter, which smooths a control signal so steps become slides. Input: the module whose control signal is smoothed Rise: seconds to glide up Fall: seconds to glide down An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Trigger Divider %'module' $nl Trigger: %'trigger' $nl Divide by: %'divide by'
block-definition.comment: Sets up a trigger divider, which passes every n-th gate. Trigger: the module whose gates are counted Divide by: 1 to 16 An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Trigger Sequencer %'module' $nl Pattern: %'pattern' $nl Tempo: %'tempo' steps/min $nl Clock: %'clock'
block-definition.comment: Sets up a trigger sequencer, a repeating pattern of gates. Pattern: one character per step; x is a gate, . is a rest Tempo: steps per minute, used when no clock is plugged in Clock: a module whose rising signal advances one step An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Note Sequencer %'module' $nl Notes: %'notes' $nl Tempo: %'tempo' steps/min $nl Clock: %'clock'
block-definition.comment: Sets up a note sequencer, a repeating row of notes sent as a pitch signal. Notes: MIDI note numbers separated by spaces; 69 is A 440, which plays an oscillator at its frequency setting Tempo: steps per minute, used when no clock is plugged in Clock: a module whose rising signal advances one step An empty jack slot unplugs that jack. An empty number counts as 0. Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.

block-definition.s: Set Keyboard %'module' $nl Source: %'source' $nl Lowest Note: %'lowest note'
block-definition.comment: Sets up a keyboard, which turns key presses into signals for other modules. Source: computer keyboard, or a MIDI device plugged into the computer (the browser asks for permission; open the dropdown again if a device is missing) Lowest Note: the MIDI note number played by the A key on the computer keyboard; 60 is middle C. The keys A S D F G H J K L ; go up the white notes and W E T Y U O P are the black notes between them. Outputs, chosen in other blocks' jack dropdowns: Keyboard: pitch, for an oscillator's control Keyboard: gate, for an ADSR's gate Keyboard: velocity, how hard a MIDI key was struck (0 to 100), for a volume's control Running the block again changes only what differs, so it may sit inside a loop.
Opens or closes the gate of an ADSR envelope by hand, like pressing and releasing a key. Opening starts the attack, closing starts the release. Drop the variable holding the ADSR into the first slot.

Reports a mix module that adds the sounds of the given modules together. Drop module variables into the slots, or type their names; click the arrows for more slots. Use the result where a module goes, for example in a filter's input or the speaker's input: set speaker input to (mix osc1 osc2)
Plugs a module into the speaker so you hear it. Drop the variable holding the module into the slot. An empty slot unplugs the speaker and silences the synth; the stop sign does the same.
Shows an oscilloscope in the middle of the stage. It draws the sound reaching the speaker, so a steady tone shows its wave shape.
Hides the oscilloscope.

Reports a saved set of oscillator settings. Use it with Snap!'s own variable block: set osc1 to (Preset 1) To store an oscillator's current settings here, use the "set preset" block. The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.

Reports a saved set of oscillator settings. Use it with Snap!'s own variable block: set osc1 to (Preset 2) To store an oscillator's current settings here, use the "set preset" block. The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.

Reports a saved set of oscillator settings. Use it with Snap!'s own variable block: set osc1 to (Preset 3) To store an oscillator's current settings here, use the "set preset" block. The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.

Reports a saved set of oscillator settings. Use it with Snap!'s own variable block: set osc1 to (Preset 4) To store an oscillator's current settings here, use the "set preset" block. The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.
Copies the settings of an oscillator into the chosen Preset block, replacing what it held. Control and trigger are stored empty. Drop the variable holding the oscillator into the second slot.
